summary: Jefferson County, PA fire tower in use by April 1922, with a visitor register past 7,500 names by 1939; the 1994 end of fire watch rests on one secondary source.

facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forestry, per a 1922 report; current agency not confirmed

events.note: Established in 1921 per onX; the earliest date we found
Sherman Seanor hired as watchman, reported April 1922
Herman Seanor described as towerman, December 1923
USGS survey mark described as set directly under the tower's center
Visitor register passed 7,500 names by September 1939
onX says the tower was used for fire detection until 1994; single secondary source

evidence.quote: has been employed as watchman on the Hays Lot fire tower

evidence.supports: more than 100 visitors on Sundays in summer 1922; Department of Forestry tower in northern Jefferson County
evidence.quote: More than 100 persons have visited the Department of Forestry's fire tower in northern Jefferson county every Sunday this summer

evidence.supports: the August 1922 report came from District Forester Zerby to the Harrisburg office
evidence.quote: according to a report sent to the Harrisburg office by District Forester Zerby, of Clarion

evidence.quote: plans to wall-in a spring and build an open fireplace for persons who desire to cook a lunch

evidence.supports: Herman Seanor described as towerman, December 1923
register past 7,500 names by September 1939; tower located between Sigel and Murderf (sic)

evidence.supports: register book kept at the tower
evidence.quote: since a register book has been kept there

evidence.supports: visitors from every state, Canada and China
evidence.quote: These people come from every state in the Union as well as an odd visitor from Canada and China

evidence.supports: survey mark set directly under the tower's center

evidence.supports: established 1921; used for forest fire detection until 1994
evidence.quote: the fire tower established in 1921 at Hays Lot, used for forest fire detection until 1994

corrections.why: The April 1922 watchman report shows the tower already in use, and onX gives 1921; no source found supports 1945

notes_for_editor: Record build year 1945 is contradicted by 1921 (onX) and an April 1922 watchman report; correction proposed. Record design (Aermotor), height (26.2 m) and standing status have no source among the pages read, so they are left out of facts. Record agency (Clear Creek State Forest) is not named in the pages read; the 1922 report names only the Department of Forestry. Current condition, access and visit details are unknown. The 1994 end of fire watch rests on one onX trail-app note. A search result mentioned a campsite called Fire Tower on Clear Creek's Callen Run tract; not verified as this tower and not used.
